Per: Justice Vivek Rusia Appellant / State of Madhya Pradesh and others have filed this writ appeal under Section 2(1) of the Madhya Pradesh Uchcha Nyayalaya (Khand Nyaypeeth Ko Appeal)
Adhiniyam, 2005 challenging the order dated 23.08.2023 passed by the Writ Court, whereby the Writ Petition No.8524 of 2014 has been allowed by setting aside the order of termination dated 12.09.2014.

sentences.text:
Facts of the case, in short, are as under:
02.
The respondent / writ petitioner was initially appointed on the post of Tendu Patta Forest Guard for three months on temporary basis vide order dated 04.06.1979.
Upon completion of 3 months period, he was appointed as NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:21399 2 WA-1310-2024 Coupe Guard vide order dated 23.11.1979.
He was further appointed as Forest Guard (trained) vide order dated 20.12.1991.
Thereafter, he was further promoted as Forester vide order dated 05.09.2006.

sentences.text: It appears that some dispute arose amongst the family members of the writ petitioner and one of them made a complaint that the writ petitioner is only 7th class pass and he produced the forged mark-sheet of class 8 th in order to secure the appointment to the post of Forest Guard.
A departmental enquiry was initiated against him and thereafter, vide order dated 12.09.2014, writ petitioner was terminated from service.
He preferred an appeal before the Chief Conservator of Forest Khandwa and when the appeal was not decided within considerable time, he approached this Court by way of writ petition.
04. The respondent / State (therein) filed the reply opposing the writ petition.
The writ petition remained pending for almost 9 years.

During these 9 years, appeal was not decided by the competent authority, therefore, the Writ Court entertained the writ petition on merit and held that under the M.P. Class III(Non-Ministerial) Forest Recruitment Rules, 1967, the minimum qualification for the post of Tendu Patta Forest Guard is 7 th class, which the petitioner possesses hence, the authority have acted in an illegal and arbitrary manner and allowed the writ petition.

sentences.text: We have heard learned Dy. Advocate General for the appellant / State at length and perused the entire record.

05. The writ petitioner was appointed in the year 1979 on the post of Tendu Patta Forest Guard,
thereafter he was made Coupe Guard and NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:21399 3 WA-1310-2024 regularly appointed on the post of Forest Guard (trained) in the year 1991.
At that time, the authority must have examined his educational qualification which is only 7th class.
The service record was prepared and on the basis of service record, he was promoted to the post of Forester on 05.09.2006.
Even at that time, the State had an occasion to examine his entire service record.

In the year 2012, one of the relative has made a complaint with mala fide intention that writ petitioner does not possess the minimum educational qualification as the mark-sheet of 8th class is forged, as a result of which he has been terminated from service.
06. The son of the writ petitioner was married to Muskan Bi D/o Dr. Arif Khan.

Some matrimonial dispute arose between husband and wife and Dr. Arif Khan lodged an FIR against writ petitioner and his son Wasim Khan that the marriage was performed by showing false higher secondary certificate examination.
The FIR was registered under Section 420/34, 467/34, 468/34 and 471/34 of IPC.
They both were tried vide Sessions Trial No.84/2011.
Vide judgment dated 25.11.2017, both have been acquitted by Second Additional Sessions Judge, Khargone.

Therefore, it is apparent that Dr. Arif Khan was behind the writ petitioner for making this false complaint against him that he produced the forged mark-sheet of 8th class in order to get the employment, whereas as discussed above, the petitioner was appointed as Tendu Patta Forest Guard for which the minimum qualification is 7th class pass.
A copy of the mark-sheet is filed as Annexure P/3 of the writ petition and there is no allegation that his mark-sheet is forged.

07. When the writ petitioner had already got an appointment on the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:21399 4 WA-1310-2024 basis of 7th class mark-sheet, thus, he was not required to The State Of Madhya Pradesh Through ... vs Ayyub Khan on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181351372/
2 produce any forged mark-sheet of class 8th.

sentences.text: Thereafter, the writ petitioner has also been promoted to the post of Forester.
In the departmental appeal, the writ petitioner has disclosed the name of other Foresters who were appointed as Forest Guard despite having qualification of class 1st, 5 th, 6 th, etc.
Hence, the writ petitioner is a victim of enmity with Dr. Arif Khan.
08. No such departmental enquiry record was produced before the Writ Court as well as in this appeal by the State.

The writ petitioner had worked from 1979 to 2012, considering 30 to 35 years,
there had been no complaint against his working.
The mark-sheet of 8t h class is not relevant when minimum qualification is only class 7th pass.

Therefore, merely on the basis of complaint,
termination was not warranted.
His working on the post of Tendu Patta Forest Guard was satisfactory, thus, he was promoted to the post of Forest Guard (trained).
Hence, the Writ Court has not committed any error by allowing the writ petition.
09. In view of the above, this Writ Appeal stands dismissed.
